intervals.quote: Brookhaven National Laboratory was established in 1947 on the eastern end of Long Island at the former site of the U.S. Army's Camp Upton.

website.note: The top-level page www.bnl.gov was not itself fetched (checked 2026-09-17); /about/ was fetched directly and is the laboratory's own official page.

name: Brookhaven National Laboratory
notes: kind is set to `accelerator_laboratory` (matching the value used for Fermilab in this atlas) because BNL's own history page centers the laboratory's identity on its accelerator complex (Cosmotron, then the Alternating Gradient Synchrotron, then RHIC; src:bnl-about-history-accelerators-page); BNL's own '/about/' page instead calls it a 'multidisciplinary laboratory', and BNL also runs non-accelerator user facilities (e.g. the National Synchrotron Light Source II) that this single-valued `kind` field does not capture. No `underground_laboratory`/`research_laboratory` framing was found that fit better given RHIC and the AGS are its historically defining machines.

The laboratory's ROR id (02ex6cf31, src:bnl-ror-record) and INSPIRE institution recid (902689, confirmed via https://inspirehep.net/api/institutions/902689 on 2026-09-17) were both found, but facility records have no external-identifier field, so neither id is shown on this record. The ROR id is used instead on the coordinates of site:bnl-upton-campus. The INSPIRE institution record is not otherwise cited, so no source entry was created for it.

RHIC (owned by this facility) ended its 25th and final run on 2026-02-06 and is being converted into the Electron-Ion Collider (src:bnl-newsroom-eic-transformation-2026); this facility record's own `status` remains `active` because the laboratory as a whole continues to operate (AGS, other user facilities, and the EIC construction project).

operator_text.note: Single verbatim sentence of the official page (the page also states that the laboratory is one of 10 national laboratories overseen and primarily funded by the U.S. Department of Energy's Office of Science).
operator_text.quote: Brookhaven Lab is managed for the Office of Science by Brookhaven Science Associates, a partnership between Stony Brook University and Battelle, and six core universities: Columbia, Cornell, Harvard, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Princeton, and Yale.
operator_text.value: Brookhaven Science Associates (a partnership of Stony Brook University and Battelle, with six core universities) for the U.S. Department of Energy's Office of Science

summary.plain: A United States national laboratory on Long Island, New York, run for the Department of Energy. It built and operated the world's first collider able to smash together beams of gold atomic nuclei and of protons with aligned spins, and it hosts other major physics, biology and materials-science facilities.
summary.technical: US Department of Energy multiprogram national laboratory (Upton, New York), managed by Brookhaven Science Associates for DOE's Office of Science; historically operated the Cosmotron (1952-1966) and the Alternating Gradient Synchrotron (commissioned 1960), and built and ran the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (2000-2026) — the first heavy-ion collider and the only polarized-proton collider — now being converted into the Electron-Ion Collider.
